contrary_evidence: Again, this is crisis relief rather than evidence of a strengthened ordinary welfare system.

evidence.claim: Shehbaz Sharif launched the 4RF for Pakistan Floods 2022, a short-, medium-, and long-term climate-resilient recovery and reconstruction framework based on the PDNA and presented as an inclusive whole-of-Pakistan approach.
evidence.title: PR No. 177 PRIME MINISTER OF PAKISTAN MUHAMMAD SHEHBAZ SHARIF LAUNCHES THE RESILIENT, RECOVERY, REHABILITATION AND RECONSTRUCTION FRAMEWORK (4RF) FOR PAKISTAN FLOODS
evidence.excerpt: Shehbaz Sharif launched the 4RF for Pakistan Floods 2022, a short-, medium-, and long-term climate-resilient recovery and reconstruction framework based on the PDNA and presented as an inclusive whole-of-Pakistan approach.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct PM launch notice with concrete policy architecture and timing.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Sharif, though the framework itself was prepared with ministries, provinces, and development partners.
contrary_evidence: A framework is not the same as measured reconstruction completion.

evidence.claim: WFP said it was expanding food assistance, malnutrition prevention, and livelihoods support for flood-affected families while the Government of Pakistan, through NDMA, was leading the response and coordinating relief.
evidence.title: WFP steps up humanitarian support to government relief efforts as Pakistan reels from devastating floods
evidence.excerpt: WFP said it was expanding food assistance, malnutrition prevention, and livelihoods support for flood-affected families while the Government of Pakistan, through NDMA, was leading the response and coordinating relief.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary WFP operational report with explicit role assignment and concrete assistance categories.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Sharif government as the leading national authority, but the response was multiactor and heavily dependent on humanitarian partners.
contrary_evidence: The same source underscores that the disaster had overwhelmed domestic capacity and required external support.

evidence.claim: WHO said Pakistan’s floods damaged or destroyed about 10 percent of health facilities, left more than eight million people needing urgent health assistance, and prompted a measles-rubella vaccination campaign that reached 1.8 million children across 38 districts.
evidence.title: Impact in 2022: Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: WHO said Pakistan’s floods damaged or destroyed about 10 percent of health facilities, left more than eight million people needing urgent health assistance, and prompted a measles-rubella vaccination campaign that reached 1.8 million children across 38 districts.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: WHO operational summary with concrete response outputs and damage estimates.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mostly crisis-response context rather than a direct PM decision, but the government was the national counterpart for the health response.
contrary_evidence: The same source makes clear that the disaster severely disrupted health services and created major unmet need.

evidence.claim: UNICEF said more than 2 million children remained out of school after floods damaged or destroyed nearly 27,000 schools and that it had established more than 500 temporary learning centres and supported teachers and children with supplies.
evidence.title: Schools for more than 2 million children in Pakistan remain inaccessible due to devastating floods
evidence.excerpt: UNICEF said more than 2 million children remained out of school after floods damaged or destroyed nearly 27,000 schools and that it had established more than 500 temporary learning centres and supported teachers and children with supplies.
evidence.source_locator: press release body and notes for editors
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary UNICEF release with specific counts and response measures.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is mostly crisis-context and partner response, not a PM-specific claim, but it defines the child-welfare stakes of the Sharif period.
contrary_evidence: The source highlights continuing educational deprivation rather than a clean welfare improvement.

evidence.claim: WHO said flooded health centres, unsafe water, damaged supplies, and disrupted access to care threatened more unsafe births and missed vaccinations, while WHO and partners were working with the government to set up temporary facilities and resupply medicines.
evidence.title: WHO Director-General's statement on Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: WHO said flooded health centres, unsafe water, damaged supplies, and disrupted access to care threatened more unsafe births and missed vaccinations, while WHO and partners were working with the government to set up temporary facilities and resupply medicines.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary WHO statement describing crisis conditions and response mechanics in real time.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mainly crisis-response context with government partnership, not a direct PM policy act.
contrary_evidence: The statement shows the depth of ongoing service disruption and unmet need.

evidence.claim: UNFPA said the floods left roughly 6.4 million people needing humanitarian assistance, including about 1.6 million women of childbearing age, and estimated that nearly 650,000 pregnant women would need maternal health services.
evidence.title: Women and girls bearing the brunt of the Pakistan Monsoon floods
evidence.excerpt: UNFPA said the floods left roughly 6.4 million people needing humanitarian assistance, including about 1.6 million women of childbearing age, and estimated that nearly 650,000 pregnant women would need maternal health services.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary UNFPA crisis assessment with concrete estimates for vulnerable groups.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is crisis context rather than a direct PM choice, but it defines the vulnerable-group burden facing the Sharif government.
contrary_evidence: The source is mostly about need and risk, not evidence of successful government protection.

evidence.claim: The PDNA called for recovery based on the principles of poor first, transparency, inclusion, and climate resilience, and said the floods affected 33 million people and could push 8.4 to 9.1 million more people below the poverty line.
evidence.title: Pakistan: Flood Damages and Economic Losses Over USD 30 billion and Reconstruction Needs Over USD 16 billion - New Assessment
evidence.excerpt: The PDNA called for recovery based on the principles of poor first, transparency, inclusion, and climate resilience, and said the floods affected 33 million people and could push 8.4 to 9.1 million more people below the poverty line.
evidence.source_locator: press release lead and human-impact section
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Joint World Bank assessment using formal post-disaster methodology and explicit social-impact estimates.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and essential for end-state evaluation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The disaster was external, but the recovery framework and distributional response were government responsibilities under Sharif.
contrary_evidence: This source is dominated by shock effects rather than successful policy delivery.

evidence.claim: The World Bank approved five projects for flood-affected Sindh, including social protection delivery, conditional cash transfers for 1.3 million mothers and children, and health services for women, girls, and children in flood-affected settlements.
evidence.title: Pakistan: World Bank Approves $1.692 Billion for 5 Projects to Support the People of Sindh in the Flood-Affected Areas
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank approved five projects for flood-affected Sindh, including social protection delivery, conditional cash transfers for 1.3 million mothers and children, and health services for women, girls, and children in flood-affected settlements.
evidence.source_locator: press release body, especially project descriptions
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary financing announcement with specific beneficiary groups and delivery mechanisms.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and relevant to the end-of-year welfare trajectory.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Sharif government’s recovery agenda, though financed and structured jointly with the World Bank and implemented at provincial level.
contrary_evidence: Province-specific recovery financing does not by itself show nationwide welfare improvement by year-end.

evidence.claim: A special court said none of the prosecution witnesses accused Shehbaz Sharif or Hamza Shehbaz of bribery, kickbacks, or corrupt practices in the Rs16 billion money laundering case, and that cogent evidence was not yet available at the bail stage.
evidence.title: Detailed order on bail confirmation: No witness accused Shehbaz, Hamza of corruption: court
evidence.excerpt: A special court said none of the prosecution witnesses accused Shehbaz Sharif or Hamza Shehbaz of bribery, kickbacks, or corrupt practices in the Rs16 billion money laundering case, and that cogent evidence was not yet available at the bail stage.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous court reporting with direct quotations from the written order; the order itself is the underlying legal source.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the target year and while Sharif was prime minister.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is a judicial assessment of allegations against Sharif and his son; it does not prove personal honesty, but it is directly relevant to the accused ruler-period record.
contrary_evidence: The judge repeatedly cautioned that the bail observations were tentative and not a merits finding.

evidence.claim: Shehbaz Sharif testified in court that he refused salary and benefits when he was chief minister of Punjab and denied committing corruption.
evidence.title: PM Shehbaz tells court he refused salary as CM during Rs16bn money laundering hearing
evidence.excerpt: Shehbaz Sharif testified in court that he refused salary and benefits when he was chief minister of Punjab and denied committing corruption.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct report of a sworn court appearance and the ruler's own statement, though it is self-serving testimony.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Sharif as his own public testimony, but it is not independent proof of honesty.
contrary_evidence: The statement was made in his own defense during a corruption case, so it is not independent corroboration.

evidence.claim: On the prime minister's advice, Ahad Cheema was appointed adviser to the PM on establishment; the report also notes his prior NAB arrest and inquiries linked to Ashiana-i-Iqbal and related cases.
evidence.title: President Alvi appoints Ahad Cheema as adviser to the PM on establishment
evidence.excerpt: On the prime minister's advice, Ahad Cheema was appointed adviser to the PM on establishment; the report also notes his prior NAB arrest and inquiries linked to Ashiana-i-Iqbal and related cases.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct contemporaneous report of a formal PM-linked appointment and the appointee's corruption-case background.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Sharif's appointment power; the appointment cuts both ways because Cheema is a professional bureaucrat but also a controversial insider with pending case history.
contrary_evidence: A career bureaucrat appointment can be read as competence-oriented, but the corruption baggage weakens the purity of that signal.

evidence.claim: An accountability court granted Shehbaz Sharif permanent exemption in the Ramzan Sugar Mills case, while the NAB allegation was that he ordered a drain to benefit mills owned by his sons and caused loss to the exchequer; Sharif responded that the project served the area and that the provincial cabinet approved it.
evidence.title: Accountability court grants PM Shehbaz permanent exemption from appearing in sugar scam case
evidence.excerpt: An accountability court granted Shehbaz Sharif permanent exemption in the Ramzan Sugar Mills case, while the NAB allegation was that he ordered a drain to benefit mills owned by his sons and caused loss to the exchequer; Sharif responded that the project served the area and that the provincial cabinet approved it.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct court reporting with the allegation and Sharif's answer on the record.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Sharif because the allegation concerns his own prior official action and his own explanation of it; the underlying guilt was not resolved in 2022.
contrary_evidence: The court action concerns exemption and allegations, not a proven finding of self-dealing; Sharif also offered a public defense.

evidence.claim: A special court declared Shehbaz Sharif's younger son Suleman a proclaimed offender in the money-laundering case and ordered his assets frozen, while the PM requested a one-time exemption from appearance.
evidence.title: PM’s son declared proclaimed offender
evidence.excerpt: A special court declared Shehbaz Sharif's younger son Suleman a proclaimed offender in the money-laundering case and ordered his assets frozen, while the PM requested a one-time exemption from appearance.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct contemporaneous court report with a concrete judicial order involving the ruler's immediate family.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is family-linked rather than a direct personal finding against Shehbaz; it matters because the chapter includes close-family benefit and tolerance, but the attribution to the PM is limited.
contrary_evidence: A son's fugitive status is not proof that the PM personally directed the misconduct.

evidence.claim: An accountability court granted permanent exemption from personal appearance to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif in the Ashiana-i-Iqbal Housing Scheme reference, where NAB alleged award of a no-bid contract and illegal gratification in the form of land.
evidence.title: PM Shehbaz gets exemption from appearance in Ashiana case
evidence.excerpt: An accountability court granted permanent exemption from personal appearance to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif in the Ashiana-i-Iqbal Housing Scheme reference, where NAB alleged award of a no-bid contract and illegal gratification in the form of land.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct court reporting on a formal corruption case and the ruler's requested exemption.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Sharif because the allegations concern his own prior government action; the case remained contested, so this is not a merits finding.
contrary_evidence: The article reports allegations rather than proof, and the exemption was procedural rather than a finding of guilt.

evidence.claim: A special court acquitted Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Hamza Shehbaz in the Rs16 billion money laundering case after the FIA told the court that no direct transaction had been made from benami accounts into their bank accounts.
evidence.title: Lahore court acquits PM Shehbaz, son Hamza in Rs16bn money laundering case
evidence.excerpt: A special court acquitted Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Hamza Shehbaz in the Rs16 billion money laundering case after the FIA told the court that no direct transaction had been made from benami accounts into their bank accounts.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct contemporaneous court report on a dispositive judicial outcome.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly relevant to Sharif because it resolves a major corruption accusation against him and his son, although it does not affirmively prove virtue beyond the case outcome.
contrary_evidence: An acquittal removes proof of this case, but it does not automatically establish broad personal integrity in all domains.

evidence.claim: The trial judge said the record was silent on any benefit to Shehbaz Sharif or Hamza from the alleged benami accounts, found no nexus between them and the accounts, and said there was no probability of conviction.
evidence.title: FIA failed to link Shehbaz, Hamza to benami accounts: judge
evidence.excerpt: The trial judge said the record was silent on any benefit to Shehbaz Sharif or Hamza from the alleged benami accounts, found no nexus between them and the accounts, and said there was no probability of conviction.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct report of a detailed written judicial verdict.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly relevant to the ruler because the verdict addresses allegations against him and his son, but it remains case-specific rather than a full integrity audit.
contrary_evidence: The verdict concerns one case and does not settle all corruption allegations about the family.

evidence.claim: The Daily Mail apologized to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, stating that he had never been accused by NAB of wrongdoing in relation to British public money or DFID grant aid and retracting the accusation that he stole aid money for earthquake victims.
evidence.title: Not accused of any wrongdoing: Daily Mail apologises to PM Shehbaz for false corruption allegation
evidence.excerpt: The Daily Mail apologized to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, stating that he had never been accused by NAB of wrongdoing in relation to British public money or DFID grant aid and retracting the accusation that he stole aid money for earthquake victims.
evidence.source_locator: lead and apology quotation in the article body
evidence.source_confidence_reason: The piece reports an explicit correction and apology from the publication, though the article is a secondary report rather than the publisher's original notice.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective correction during 2022; relevant because it concerns a major corruption accusation against Sharif.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is not a ruler action, but it is an independent correction that materially weakens one prominent public corruption allegation against him.
contrary_evidence: The apology concerns one historical allegation and does not resolve the separate domestic money-laundering cases.

evidence.claim: The ECP data released in 2022 showed Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's assets at about Rs246 million, including London property, a small bank balance, liabilities, and a loan from his son Suleman.
evidence.title: ECP releases data of assets owned by PM Shehbaz, Imran Khan, Zardari, and others
evidence.excerpt: The ECP data released in 2022 showed Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's assets at about Rs246 million, including London property, a small bank balance, liabilities, and a loan from his son Suleman.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: The report is based on an official ECP asset disclosure, but the page is a media summary rather than the underlying filing.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Sharif's own disclosure and relevant to transparency, though it does not by itself prove clean governance or the absence of conflicts.
contrary_evidence: Public asset disclosure is positive for transparency but not proof that no hidden conflicts or family entanglements existed.

evidence.claim: Shehbaz Sharif appointed a multi-party coalition cabinet that immediately focused on stabilizing the economy and restarting IMF talks.
evidence.title: Pakistan's new PM picks coalition cabinet after Khan ousted
evidence.excerpt: Shehbaz Sharif appointed a multi-party coalition cabinet that immediately focused on stabilizing the economy and restarting IMF talks.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire carried by a reputable outlet; specific date and named appointments are clear.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct PM action, though coalition bargaining limited full control.
contrary_evidence: Coalition partners had divergent views on timing and priorities.

evidence.claim: The finance minister said the new government would cut expenditures and development funds to revive the IMF programme.
evidence.title: Pakistan to cut expenditures, development funds to revive IMF programme
evidence.excerpt: The finance minister said the new government would cut expenditures and development funds to revive the IMF programme.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire with direct quote from the finance minister; credible but hosted on a secondary outlet.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly tied to Sharif's government, though the fiscal crisis was inherited.
contrary_evidence: The article also shows the government was reacting to a pre-existing balance-of-payments crisis.

evidence.claim: The budget raised taxes on the rich, restricted car purchases, targeted a 4.9 percent fiscal deficit, and had already raised fuel prices by 40 percent.
evidence.title: Pakistan to raise taxes on rich, ban some car buying to secure IMF bailout
evidence.excerpt: The budget raised taxes on the rich, restricted car purchases, targeted a 4.9 percent fiscal deficit, and had already raised fuel prices by 40 percent.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire with direct budget reporting and specific numeric targets.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct policy under Sharif's government, though heavily IMF-constrained.
contrary_evidence: The same article notes the economy was already in a balance-of-payments crisis.

evidence.claim: Pakistan took important measures, and the IMF prioritized steadfast FY23 budget implementation, a market-determined exchange rate, prudent monetary policy, social safety, and SOE/governance reforms.
evidence.title: IMF Executive Board Completes the Combined Seventh, and Eighth Reviews of the Extended Fund Facility for Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: Pakistan took important measures, and the IMF prioritized steadfast FY23 budget implementation, a market-determined exchange rate, prudent monetary policy, social safety, and SOE/governance reforms.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary IMF press release with program details and official approval outcome.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong but mediated by the IMF program and inherited macro crisis.
contrary_evidence: The same release says FY22 policies produced overheating, deficits, and reserve erosion.

evidence.claim: Pakistan’s economy was expected to grow only 2 percent in FY23 and inflation around 23 percent, with floods, tight monetary conditions, and high inflation weighing on performance.
evidence.title: World Bank: Pakistan’s Economy Slows Down While Inflation Rises Amid Catastrophic Floods
evidence.excerpt: Pakistan’s economy was expected to grow only 2 percent in FY23 and inflation around 23 percent, with floods, tight monetary conditions, and high inflation weighing on performance.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary World Bank press release with explicit dated projections and causal framing.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mostly contextual: it reflects inherited constraints and shocks more than Sharif's independent control.
contrary_evidence: The report also says targeted relief and reforms were still available policy levers.

evidence.claim: The PDNA estimated large flood damages and reconstruction needs, called for a poor-first, transparent, inclusive recovery, and said the government was providing immediate relief while aiming at macroeconomic stability.
evidence.title: Pakistan: Flood Damages and Economic Losses Over USD 30 billion and Reconstruction Needs Over USD 16 billion - New Assessment
evidence.excerpt: The PDNA estimated large flood damages and reconstruction needs, called for a poor-first, transparent, inclusive recovery, and said the government was providing immediate relief while aiming at macroeconomic stability.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary World Bank assessment with explicit recovery principles and quantified damage estimates.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly attributable through government relief design and response, but heavily constrained by disaster magnitude and donor reliance.
contrary_evidence: The assessment says losses and poverty impacts were still increasing and external support would be essential.

evidence.claim: Annual CPI inflation was 23.8 percent in November, reserves were barely one month of imports, and the IMF was still pressing for expenditure cuts and a recovery plan.
evidence.title: Pakistan's consumer price inflation slows to 23.8%
evidence.excerpt: Annual CPI inflation was 23.8 percent in November, reserves were barely one month of imports, and the IMF was still pressing for expenditure cuts and a recovery plan.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire with official inflation data and contemporaneous macro context.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mostly outcome context, not a clean measure of Sharif's direct control; inherited crisis and shocks mattered heavily.
contrary_evidence: The article notes policy tightening and some expectation of marginal inflation easing.

evidence.claim: Five World Bank projects supported flood recovery, housing reconstruction, crop restoration, social protection delivery, and health services for mothers and children, including cash transfers and strengthened disaster-response capacity.
evidence.title: Pakistan: World Bank Approves $1.692 Billion for 5 Projects to Support the People of Sindh in the Flood-Affected Areas
evidence.excerpt: Five World Bank projects supported flood recovery, housing reconstruction, crop restoration, social protection delivery, and health services for mothers and children, including cash transfers and strengthened disaster-response capacity.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary World Bank announcement with concrete project terms and funding amounts.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but relevant: the Sharif government was the implementing counterpart, though execution depended on the Bank and provinces.
contrary_evidence: This is implementation architecture more than proof of completed outcomes by year-end.

evidence.claim: After the Islamabad High Court said successive chief executives had given tacit approval to enforced disappearances, the federal government formed a seven-member committee under the law minister to deliberate policy, and the PM was briefed on the issue.
evidence.title: Govt forms committee to 'deliberate policy' on enforced disappearances
evidence.excerpt: After the Islamabad High Court said successive chief executives had given tacit approval to enforced disappearances, the federal government formed a seven-member committee under the law minister to deliberate policy, and the PM was briefed on the issue.
evidence.source_locator: Dawn summary of the IHC order and ministry notification
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous report of a formal government notification and court order; direct PM-level ordering is still indirect.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Shows Sharif's government responding after judicial notice; it does not prove he personally designed the disappearance policy.
contrary_evidence: The underlying practice predates Sharif and the operational actors are not named here.

evidence.claim: NCHR said the IHC treated enforced disappearances as a 'seemingly undeclared tacit policy of the state' and welcomed the court's order holding chief executives and interior ministers, past and present, accountable, while also welcoming the government's committee on the issue.
evidence.title: NCHR Statement on IHC Ruling on Enforced Disappearances
evidence.publisher: National Commission for Human Rights Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: NCHR said the IHC treated enforced disappearances as a 'seemingly undeclared tacit policy of the state' and welcomed the court's order holding chief executives and interior ministers, past and present, accountable, while also welcoming the government's committee on the issue.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official statutory human-rights body summarizing the court ruling and government response.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong for attribution of Sharif's government as the addressed authority; weak for proving personal operational direction.
contrary_evidence: The statement does not identify which security actors carried out individual disappearances.

evidence.claim: Amnesty reported that families of the disappeared and activists protesting enforced disappearances were met with state violence, intimidation, arbitrary detention, and arrest for peaceful assembly.
evidence.title: Pakistan: Braving the Storm: Enforced disappearances and the right to protest in Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: Amnesty reported that families of the disappeared and activists protesting enforced disappearances were met with state violence, intimidation, arbitrary detention, and arrest for peaceful assembly.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent rights report with a clear 2022 scope and specific abuse pattern.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Supports a state-abuse pattern under Sharif's term, but it does not by itself prove his personal ordering of each incident.
contrary_evidence: The report attributes the abuses to state forces generally, not to Sharif personally.

evidence.claim: The Islamabad High Court ordered the federal government and interior secretary to appoint an inquiry officer into allegations that PTI leader Shahbaz Gill was tortured in police custody, and ordered SSP-level supervision to ensure no further torture.
evidence.title: IHC orders inquiry into claims of torture on Gill
evidence.excerpt: The Islamabad High Court ordered the federal government and interior secretary to appoint an inquiry officer into allegations that PTI leader Shahbaz Gill was tortured in police custody, and ordered SSP-level supervision to ensure no further torture.
evidence.source_locator: report of the IHC order and the court's directions
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Court order summarized by a mainstream local outlet; the underlying court record is the stronger source but was not directly accessible here.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly implicates the police custody chain during Sharif's government, but not a proven personal order by Sharif.
contrary_evidence: Police and government officials denied torture; the dispute remained under inquiry.

evidence.claim: NCHR said its Adiala Jail inquiry found 74% of interviewed inmates alleging torture and 100% reporting financial extortion for access to basic facilities, and the court ordered the report shared with the PM and cabinet for immediate action against responsible public servants.
evidence.title: Press Release: NCHR Inquiry Report on Custodial Torture at Central Jail (Adiala), Rawalpindi
evidence.publisher: National Commission for Human Rights Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: NCHR said its Adiala Jail inquiry found 74% of interviewed inmates alleging torture and 100% reporting financial extortion for access to basic facilities, and the court ordered the report shared with the PM and cabinet for immediate action against responsible public servants.
evidence.source_locator: paragraphs describing the inquiry findings and court directions
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official inquiry report announcement with concrete findings and a court-ordered response chain.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong for prison administration under the federal government; still indirect for naming Sharif as the actor behind abuse.
contrary_evidence: The report describes jail conditions and responsible public servants, not a personal PM order.

evidence.claim: President Arif Alvi wrote to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressing deep concern over harassment of journalists, citing arrests, beatings, harassment, and sedition cases meant to create fear and terror, and urging immediate remedial action and protection from security agencies.
evidence.title: Alvi concerned over treatment of journalists
evidence.excerpt: President Arif Alvi wrote to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressing deep concern over harassment of journalists, citing arrests, beatings, harassment, and sedition cases meant to create fear and terror, and urging immediate remedial action and protection from security agencies.
evidence.source_locator: Dawn summary of the president's letter
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous report of a direct written notice to Sharif from the head of state.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is direct notice to Sharif and his government; it still does not prove he personally directed the harassment.
contrary_evidence: The letter is a warning and request, not proof of authorial control over every abuse.

evidence.claim: NCHR launched a complaint cell for women journalists after a consultative meeting with women journalists from across Pakistan, citing online violence, harassment, attack risks, and censorship against women reporters.
evidence.title: NCHR launches complaint cell for women journalists
evidence.excerpt: NCHR launched a complaint cell for women journalists after a consultative meeting with women journalists from across Pakistan, citing online violence, harassment, attack risks, and censorship against women reporters.
evidence.source_locator: article body describing the launch and the consultative meeting
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous local reporting of an official human-rights initiative with specific abuse descriptions.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Useful as evidence of a documented abuse environment and institutional response; the PM link remains indirect unless paired with the president's letter.
contrary_evidence: The article does not establish direct PM-level authorship of the abuse campaigns.

evidence.claim: NCHR's minority report said nearly half of reserved minority posts were vacant, 80% of non-Muslims in filled posts were in BPS 01-04, and the Ministry of Human Rights sent letters to provincial chief secretaries directing them to protect minority rights.
evidence.title: NCHR launches fact finding report on minority rights
evidence.excerpt: NCHR's minority report said nearly half of reserved minority posts were vacant, 80% of non-Muslims in filled posts were in BPS 01-04, and the Ministry of Human Rights sent letters to provincial chief secretaries directing them to protect minority rights.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official news service reporting a government-linked rights report and subsequent ministry action to provinces.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong for provincial policy action under Sharif's federal government; weak for proving personal day-to-day management.
contrary_evidence: The report reflects longstanding structural discrimination and does not isolate Sharif as the sole cause.
